story_description: Implement bidirectional JSON-RPC communication for Codex CLI tool approval requests. Unlike Claude Code which uses pre-approval via --allowedTools flags, Codex app-server sends runtime REQUESTS that require synchronous RESPONSES with matching IDs.
task: T004: CodexApprovalFlow - Tool Approval Request/Response Handling
task_description: Implement CodexApprovalFlow class that receives JSON-RPC tool approval requests from Codex app-server, maps them to ToolRiskLevel, integrates with ToolApprovalPipeline, and sends properly formatted JSON-RPC responses with matching request IDs.
atom_description: Build CodexApprovalFlow.swift handling codex/requestApproval/commandExecution and codex/requestApproval/fileChange JSON-RPC methods. Map commandExecution to high risk, fileChange to medium risk, others to low risk. Integrate with existing ToolApprovalPipeline for decision flow. Return JSON-RPC response with matching ID and decision accept/reject.
problem_statement: Codex app-server uses a fundamentally different approval model than Claude Code. Instead of pre-approving tools via CLI flags, Codex sends JSON-RPC REQUESTS at runtime asking for permission to execute commands or modify files. The client MUST respond with a JSON-RPC response containing the same request ID and a decision. Without this bidirectional protocol, Codex will hang waiting for responses. We need to: (1) parse incoming JSON-RPC requests, (2) map approval types to ToolRiskLevel for consistent UX, (3) integrate with ToolApprovalPipeline for user decisions, and (4) format and send JSON-RPC responses.

assumptions: Codex app-server sends well-formed JSON-RPC 2.0 requests
Request ID is always a number (per Codex protocol, not string)
Params object contains command or file_path fields as appropriate
ToolApprovalPipeline is initialized and ready to receive requests
User will see approval UI rendered by existing ToolApprovalCard component
Response must be sent on same channel that received request
constraints: Must use JSON-RPC 2.0 format for responses (id, result, no error on success)
Response ID must exactly match request ID (numeric, not string conversion)
Must not block Codex communication channel while waiting for approval
Must integrate cleanly with existing ToolApprovalPipeline actor
Must handle rapid sequential requests without race conditions
Must support cancellation without leaving orphaned requests in pipeline
Memory usage for pending requests must stay bounded
functional_requirements: FR1: CodexApprovalFlow shall parse incoming JSON-RPC requests and extract id, method, and params
FR2: CodexApprovalFlow shall identify codex/requestApproval/commandExecution as shell command approval
FR3: CodexApprovalFlow shall identify codex/requestApproval/fileChange as file modification approval
FR4: CodexApprovalFlow shall map commandExecution to ToolRiskLevel.high
FR5: CodexApprovalFlow shall map fileChange to ToolRiskLevel.medium
FR6: CodexApprovalFlow shall map unknown approval methods to ToolRiskLevel.low
FR7: CodexApprovalFlow shall create ToolRequestEvent with mapped risk level and extracted params
FR8: CodexApprovalFlow shall submit ToolRequestEvent to ToolApprovalPipeline.submitRequest
FR9: CodexApprovalFlow shall await ToolDecisionEvent from pipeline before responding
FR10: CodexApprovalFlow shall format JSON-RPC response with matching numeric id
FR11: CodexApprovalFlow shall set result.decision to accept when ToolDecisionEvent.decision is approved or alwaysAllow
FR12: CodexApprovalFlow shall set result.decision to reject when ToolDecisionEvent.decision is rejected
FR13: CodexApprovalFlow shall send formatted response via output callback
FR14: CodexApprovalFlow shall timeout and reject if no decision within 5 minutes
FR15: CodexApprovalFlow shall support cancellation via Swift Task cancellation
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: CodexApprovalFlow shall process incoming request within 50ms before blocking on decision
NFR2: Response formatting and sending shall complete within 10ms after decision received
NFR3: Memory per pending request shall not exceed 1KB
NFR4: CodexApprovalFlow shall handle at least 10 concurrent pending requests
NFR5: All operations shall be thread-safe using Swift actors or structured concurrency
NFR6: Logging shall include request ID for debugging JSON-RPC correlation
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create CodexApprovalFlow.swift file in Blaze/Sources/Engine/Codex/ directory
Step 2: Define CodexApprovalRequest struct with id (Int), method (String), params (dictionary)
Step 3: Define CodexApprovalResponse struct with id (Int), result (dictionary containing decision)
Step 4: Define CodexApprovalFlow actor with pipeline reference and response callback
Step 5: Add private pendingRequests dictionary mapping request ID to Task for cancellation
Step 6: Implement parseRequest(_ jsonData: Data) throws -> CodexApprovalRequest
Step 7: Implement mapMethodToRiskLevel(_ method: String) -> ToolRiskLevel with switch statement
Step 8: Map codex/requestApproval/commandExecution to ToolRiskLevel.high
Step 9: Map codex/requestApproval/fileChange to ToolRiskLevel.medium
Step 10: Map default case to ToolRiskLevel.low
Step 11: Implement createToolRequest(from codexRequest: CodexApprovalRequest) -> ToolRequestEvent
Step 12: Extract tool name from method (commandExecution -> Bash, fileChange -> Write)
Step 13: Extract scope from params (command text or file_path)
Step 14: Implement handleRequest(_ data: Data) async method as main entry point
Step 15: Parse request, create ToolRequestEvent, submit to pipeline
Step 16: Await decision with timeout using Task.sleep and withThrowingTaskGroup
Step 17: Format response based on decision outcome
Step 18: Implement formatResponse(requestId: Int, decision: ToolDecision) -> Data
Step 19: Create JSON object with id matching request, result.decision as accept or reject
Step 20: Serialize to Data using JSONSerialization
Step 21: Call response callback with formatted data
Step 22: Implement cancel(requestId: Int) to terminate pending request task
Step 23: Implement cancelAll() for session cleanup
Step 24: Add logging at each step with request ID for correlation

edge_cases: Edge case 1: Malformed JSON in request - log error, do not crash, skip request
Edge case 2: Missing id field in request - log warning, cannot respond without ID
Edge case 3: Missing method field - reject with default response
Edge case 4: Unknown method type - map to low risk and proceed
Edge case 5: Duplicate request ID while previous still pending - cancel previous, handle new
Edge case 6: Request arrives after session ended - ignore, log warning
Edge case 7: Pipeline returns decision after response callback fails - log error, continue
Edge case 8: User approves with alwaysAllow - respond with accept, rule added by pipeline
Edge case 9: Timeout occurs - send reject response, clean up pending state
Edge case 10: Task cancelled during pipeline await - propagate cancellation cleanly
failure_modes: FM1: JSON parsing fails - log error with raw data snippet, skip request silently
FM2: Pipeline submission fails - send reject response, log error
FM3: Response callback throws - log error, remove from pending, continue
FM4: Timeout without user action - send reject response with timeout rationale
FM5: Memory pressure with many pending - oldest requests timeout first
FM6: Task cancellation race - use actor isolation to prevent data races
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Engine/Codex/CodexApprovalFlow.swift. Remove integration from CodexEngineAdapter.swift. Codex sessions will hang on approval requests without this component, so rollback effectively disables Codex approval flow until reimplemented.

notes: This is the critical protocol adapter between Codex JSON-RPC approval model and Blaze ToolApprovalPipeline. The key insight is that Codex REQUESTS require RESPONSES with matching IDs - this is fundamentally different from Claude pre-approval model. Response ID must be numeric to match Codex expectations.

risks: Risk 1: JSON-RPC ID type mismatch (string vs number) could break Codex communication
Risk 2: Race condition if multiple requests arrive before first decision made
Risk 3: ToolApprovalPipeline blocking could cause Codex timeout
Risk 4: Memory leak if pending requests not cleaned up on session end
Risk 5: Protocol version mismatch with future Codex updates
mitigations: Mitigation 1: Enforce numeric ID in parsing and response, add explicit test case
Mitigation 2: Use Swift actor isolation to serialize request handling
Mitigation 3: Add timeout with configurable duration, reject on timeout
Mitigation 4: Implement cancelAll in session cleanup path
Mitigation 5: Version check Codex binary and warn on unsupported versions
risk_register.blast_radius: Limited to Codex sessions only. Claude and Gemini sessions unaffected. Failure causes Codex to hang on approval, recoverable by session restart.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If approval protocol fails, disable Codex integration with warning message. Users can use Codex CLI directly in terminal as workaround.
